issue.title: Hero image appears distorted due to over-compressed asset
issue.body:
## Problem

The hero image on the published landing page appears soft and distorted compared with the original artwork.

## Findings

- The published JPEG retains the original 1536 × 1024 dimensions but is only about 30 KB.
- The original PNG is approximately 1.95 MB and preserves the intended detail.
- The CSS uses `background-size: cover`, which preserves aspect ratio, so the visible degradation comes from the heavily compressed image asset rather than layout stretching.

## Proposed fix

Regenerate the existing `assets/akme-repair-hero.jpg` from the original PNG at high JPEG quality, preserving the existing path, dimensions, composition, and CSS behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- The hero remains 1536 × 1024 with its original aspect ratio.
- Fine detail in the technician, drill, toolbox, and workbench is restored.
- Only the hero asset changes.
- The replacement image validates as a complete JPEG and remains reasonably optimized for web delivery.
issue.display_title: Hero image appears distorted due to over-compressed asset

issue.title: Add baseline repository and website protections
issue.body:
## Problem

The repository protects `main` from direct destructive changes, but it has no automated validation for the static site and no standard contribution or vulnerability-reporting files. Broken asset references, encoding artifacts, invalid JavaScript, or a severely degraded hero image could therefore reach GitHub Pages without an automated signal.

## Proposed protections

- Add a least-privilege GitHub Actions workflow for the static site.
- Validate required files, local asset references, text encoding, page metadata, JavaScript syntax, and hero-image integrity/size.
- Add a pull request checklist.
- Add CODEOWNERS routing for the current maintainer.
- Add a SECURITY.md policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Validation passes against the restored hero asset and fails against the degraded asset.
- The workflow has read-only repository permissions.
- All repository-file changes arrive through a linked pull request.

Account-level settings such as secret protection and action pinning are tracked in the related PR description but are applied directly because they cannot be represented as repository files.
issue.display_title: Add baseline repository and website protections

pull_request.body:
## What changed

- Replaced corrupted punctuation, arrows, checkmarks, service icons, and the copyright symbol with encoding-independent HTML character references.
- Escaped the ampersand in the trust strip for valid HTML.

## Why

The published HTML contained mojibake sequences caused by text being decoded with the wrong character encoding. Those sequences appeared visibly on the GitHub Pages site.

## Impact

Visitors will see the intended apostrophes, quotation marks, arrows, icons, em dashes, and copyright symbol across the landing page.

## Validation

- Confirmed no mojibake markers remain in `index.html`.
- Confirmed every expected HTML character reference is present.
- Ran Git whitespace and patch validation successfully.

pull_request.body:
## Discussion and reason

Closes #2.

The linked issue documents the visible distortion, source-file comparison, root cause, and acceptance criteria. The published JPEG retained the correct 1536 × 1024 dimensions but contained only about 30 KB of image data, causing severe quality loss despite correct CSS aspect-ratio handling.

## What changed

- Regenerated `assets/akme-repair-hero.jpg` directly from the original 1.95 MB PNG.
- Preserved the existing 1536 × 1024 dimensions, composition, file path, and page styling.
- Used a high-quality, complete JPEG encoding suitable for web delivery.

## User impact

The hero image now preserves fine detail in the technician, drill, toolbox, and workbench instead of appearing smeared or distorted.

## Validation

- Confirmed the replacement is a valid, complete 1536 × 1024 RGB JPEG.
- Increased the hero asset from 30,012 bytes to 272,548 bytes.
- Visually inspected the regenerated asset against the original source.
- Confirmed the PR changes only `assets/akme-repair-hero.jpg`.

pull_request.body:
## Discussion and reason

Closes #4.

Issue #4 documents the missing validation and repository-governance baseline. This branch is based on the hero-quality fix from #3 so the new image-integrity check starts from a valid asset. Keep this PR in draft until #3 merges; GitHub will then remove the overlapping hero change from this diff automatically.

## What changed

- Added a least-privilege `validate-site` workflow with a full-SHA-pinned checkout action.
- Added dependency-free checks for required files, local references, encoding artifacts, page metadata, JavaScript syntax, and hero-image integrity/size.
- Added a pull request checklist.
- Added CODEOWNERS routing to the current maintainer.
- Added a vulnerability-reporting policy.

## Repository settings applied

- Corrected the merge queue to use squash commits.
- Enabled SHA pinning for Actions.
- Enabled private vulnerability reporting.
- Enabled Dependabot security updates and malware alerts.
- Enabled secret scanning and push protection.
- Enabled auto-merge and automatic deletion of merged branches.

## Validation

- The validator fails against the degraded 30 KB/incomplete hero JPEG.
- The validator passes against the restored hero asset from #3.
- `script.js` passes Node syntax validation.
- `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors.

## Risk

Low. The workflow is read-only, dependency-free, timeout-limited, and uses a pinned third-party action.
